Cylindrical invisibility cloaks with simplified material parameters are inherently visible.
The zeroth-order cylindrical wave passes through the simplified cloak as if it were a homogeneous isotropic medium.
High-order cylindrical waves experience finite scattering in the simplified cloak.
The scattering coefficient for the zeroth-order wave converges to 0.867 as the outer radius increases.
The transmission coefficient for the zeroth-order wave converges to 1 as the outer radius increases.
The effective refractive index for the zeroth-order wave is n_eff = b / (b - a).
The simplified cloak cannot completely shield objects from electromagnetic detection.
The coordinate transformation method requires anisotropic, spatially varying material parameters.
Some material parameters in the ideal cloak have infinite values at the inner boundary.
The simplified cloak uses only one gradient material parameter and avoids infinite values.
The finite-element method was used for numerical simulations.
COMSOL software was used to perform the numerical calculations.
The cloak's performance is sensitive to the position of the inner boundary.
Even a small mis-location of the inner boundary leads to significant field leakage.
The simplified cloak inherits some properties of the ideal cloak but has higher overall scattering.
The scattering of high-order waves does not converge to zero, even for very thick cloak walls.
The zeroth-order wave is not effectively cloaked by simplified material parameters.
The cloak's visibility is due to the penetration of the monopole field component.
Detection of objects inside the cloak can be enhanced by using a source with maximum energy in the monopole component.
The cloak's material parameters are azimuthally invariant.
The wave equation inside the cloak is altered by the simplification of material parameters.
The scattering problem is solved by matching tangential fields at layer interfaces.
The transmission and scattering of the cloak are examined for each individual cylindrical wave order.
The cloak's performance was examined for different values of the outer radius b.
The cloak's inner radius a was fixed at 0.1m in the simulations.
